gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the separate-reel setups from the makers' own stores: the cheapest working Active 2.0 setup (tool $319.99, M-Series reel $269.99, rinse kit with gun, lance and 50 ft hose $232.72) costs $822.70, an Active 2.3 setup built the same way costs $1,052.70, and the Kränzle K1322TS plus a Coxreels hand-crank reel costs $1,519.96 before any hose. The Grandfalls Pro costs $594.99 and the Lite Pro $439.99, and both come with a 100 ft auto-retracting hose.
standout_why: I compared against progaragegear.com (cited), cleangearlab.com, fixlinelocal.com and bobvila.com (cited). progaragegear gives '~$400 Total' for Active 2.0 plus a reel, which today's Active store prices contradict ($709.97 at the very least for tool, reel and hose, and $822.70 once you add a gun), and it never squares that figure with its own '$1,500–$3,000+' Route B. cleangearlab prices only the Active 2.0 pump (about $200) and gives no setup total. fixlinelocal prices only Giraffe models, and its Pro, G20 and Plus prices ($629.99, $249.99, $379.99) are above what the Giraffe store shows today. Bob Vila says only 'around $700' for the Pro. ChatGPT's own range of '$700–$1,100+' for Active 2.3 plus a reel is roughly right, but no page it got shows the parts behind that total, and none mentions that the Coxreels reel paired with the Kränzle is hand-crank.
decides: This supports an all-in-one Grandfalls as the pick for most garages. The Lite Pro ($439.99) and Pro ($594.99) cost about half of the cheapest working Active 2.3 reel setup ($1,052.70) and come with an auto-retracting 100 ft hose. The modular route makes sense only for buyers who will pay about $1,050 to $1,520 or more for higher flow: Active rates the 2.3 at 2.3 GPM at about 1,100 PSI, and fixlinelocal lists the Pro's store-rated figure as 1.2 GPM. It also brings Giraffe's own high-flow Crossfalls Ultra ($949.99, 2.6 GPM, 50 ft retractable hose) into play, which undercuts the Active 2.3 setup for buyers who want both flow and auto-retract.
